investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-16T00:27–00:34Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 133–148 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new remote-agent pod. With zero schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod submission stalls indefinitely, preventing VM provisioning and causing all three remote-agents eval checks to fail with identical scheduler rejection messages. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), and those 2 are already at capacity. This is a cluster topology constraint, not a code defect.

[Medium confidence] Cluster has not scaled out: no new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes were added to absorb demand, and the scheduler confirms preemption is not helpful (no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes).

[Low confidence] A recent workload spike or leaked remote-agent pod (e.g., from a prior eval run that did not clean up) may be holding the remaining VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new scheduling.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-16T00:29–00:34Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~133–148 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected signal, and no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in this packet to confirm a broader production outage.

Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 133–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-16T00:27–00:34Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 133–148 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new remote-agent pod. With zero schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod submission stalls indefinitely, preventing VM provisioning and causing all three remote-agents eval checks to fail with identical scheduler rejection messages. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), and those 2 are already at capacity. This is a cluster topology constraint, not a code defect.

[Medium confidence] Cluster has not scaled out: no new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes were added to absorb demand, and the scheduler confirms preemption is not helpful (no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes).

[Low confidence] A recent workload spike or leaked remote-agent pod (e.g., from a prior eval run that did not clean up) may be holding the remaining VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new scheduling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 3 Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 00:29 and 00:34 UTC on 2026-08-16 with an identical Kubernetes Unschedulable error: the 6-node production cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent, and consequently zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were already fully allocated (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 133–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry this resource are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to only 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If affinity rules changed or node labels drifted, the effective pool may have shrunk.

Tertiary — concurrent eval or workload contention: if multiple eval runs or production workloads simultaneously requested kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the 2-node pool could be transiently exhausted. The sequential timing of the three failing checks (00:29, 00:32, 00:34) is consistent with each run consuming or waiting on the same constrained resource.

Lower confidence — VM pool not scaled to meet demand: the cluster may not have autoscaling configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, or the autoscaler did not provision new nodes within the eval timeout window.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the current kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity on the 2 eligible production nodes to determine if the pool is still exhausted or has recovered.
Determine whether the 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector are intentionally excluded (e.g., different machine type or zone) or whether label drift has incorrectly shrunk the schedulable pool.

If the pool is persistently exhausted, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool needs to be scaled up (more nodes or higher per-node VM capacity) to accommodate concurrent eval and production workloads.
Check whether cluster autoscaling is configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes and, if so, why it did not provision additional capacity within the ~150-second eval timeout window.

Review whether concurrent eval runs or production remote agent workloads were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure (00:29–00:34 UTC on 2026-08-16) to assess whether this is a contention or a baseline capacity problem.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 185), so this check does not itself trigger an outage threshold; however, remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183–184) and both also failed, which may trigger the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold for the remote-agents feature.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show available capacity at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.
If the pod's node affinity/selector rules are confirmed unchanged and all 6 nodes match them, the 4-node exclusion would point to a node label drift or taint rather than a configuration issue.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient capacity exhaustion rather than a persistent misconfiguration.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a subsequent run, the failure would be isolated to the runtime check rather than a shared scheduling bottleneck.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is registered on any node in the cluster, the root cause would shift to a missing node configuration rather than exhaustion of an existing pool.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (allocatable vs. allocated) and alerts when headroom falls below a minimum threshold, providing earlier warning before pod scheduling fails.

Add a scheduling-latency eval that measures time-to-schedule for a remote agent pod and warns when it exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure before it causes full Unschedulable failures.

Add an eval that validates node affinity/selector coverage — confirming that at least N nodes in the cluster match the remote agent pod's scheduling requirements — to catch label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Consider a canary eval that attempts a lightweight remote agent pod creation on a fixed schedule (e.g., every 5 minutes) with a short timeout, so capacity exhaustion is detected faster than the current full runtime eval cycle.
